content: The content provided appears to be a detailed list of references, guidelines, and resources related to various health topics, including mental health, substance use, school health, infectious diseases, and public health interventions. 1. The WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) provides guidance on addressing mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in non-specialized health settings. 2. Tobacco use prevention is highlighted as a critical entry point for developing health-promoting schools, as outlined in WHO's school health information series. 3. A toolkit has been developed to deliver the 5 A's and 5 R's brief tobacco interventions for tuberculosis patients in primary care settings. 4. Evidence-based strategies for preventing youth violence are summarized in WHO's comprehensive overview. 5. The INSPIRE framework outlines seven strategies to end violence against children, emphasizing evidence-based interventions. 6. WHO provides recommendations for public health approaches to brief sexuality-related communication. 7. Health-promoting schools are tasked with preventing HIV/AIDS, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and related discrimination, as detailed in WHO's school health series. 8. WHO clinical guidelines address the response to children and adolescents who have been sexually abused, offering evidence-based recommendations for care. 9. 10. 11. Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection are available in WHO's second edition of public health recommendations. 12. Community management of opioid overdose is addressed in WHO's guidelines, emphasizing harm reduction strategies. 13. WHO provides guidelines for the prevention and control of noncommunicable diseases in primary healthcare settings, particularly in low-resource environments. 14. Updated guidelines for pediatric emergency triage, assessment, and treatment focus on the care of critically ill children. 15. WHO's Save Lives technical package offers a comprehensive approach to road safety. 16. The World Report on Road Traffic Injury Prevention highlights strategies to reduce road traffic injuries globally. 17. Burn prevention success stories and lessons learned are documented in WHO's publication. 18. The physical school environment is identified as a vital component of health-promoting schools in WHO's school health series. 19. Recommendations for managing common childhood conditions, including pneumonia, dysentery, and severe acute malnutrition, are provided in WHO's technical updates. 20. WHO and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) offer a basic emergency care workbook for managing acutely ill and injured patients. 21. WHO guidelines promote the use of safety-engineered syringes for intramuscular, intradermal, and subcutaneous injections in healthcare settings. 22. Persistent pain in children is addressed through WHO's pharmacological treatment guidelines for children with medical illnesses. 23. Interventions for children with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) include both pharmacological and non-pharmacological approaches, as outlined in WHO's evidence-based recommendations. 24. WHO's updated mhGAP guidelines provide evidence-based interventions for mental, neurological, and substance use disorders. 25. WHO offers recommendations for managing diarrhea and pneumonia in HIV-infected infants and children through integrated childhood illness management. 26. A training guide for recognizing neglected tropical diseases through skin changes is available for frontline health workers. 27. WHO guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of leprosy provide comprehensive recommendations for healthcare providers. 28. A guide for eradicating yaws is available for program managers, emphasizing effective strategies for disease elimination. 29. WHO's guidelines for dengue diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and control are presented in a new edition. 30. Updated guidelines for malaria treatment are provided in WHO's third edition, focusing on evidence-based practices. 31. WHO's informal consultation on fever management in peripheral healthcare settings reviews global evidence and practices. 32. National tuberculosis programs are guided by WHO's recommendations for managing tuberculosis in children. 33. WHO provides a resource for treating measles in children, emphasizing evidence-based care. 34. Consolidated guidelines on sexual and reproductive health and rights for women living with HIV are available from WHO. 35. WHO offers an integrated approach to the nutritional care of HIV-infected children aged 6 months to 14 years. 36. Updated guidelines on managing severe acute malnutrition in infants and children are provided by WHO. 37. Comprehensive cervical cancer prevention and control strategies are outlined in WHO's guidance note. 38. WHO recommends 36 months of isoniazid preventive therapy for adults and adolescents living with HIV in high TB and HIV prevalence settings. 39. 40. Daily iron supplementation guidelines for infants, children, and adult women are provided by WHO to address micronutrient deficiencies. 41. WHO guidelines on the use of multiple micronutrient powders for food fortification in children are available. 42. Caregiver skills training for managing developmental disorders in children is outlined in WHO's evidence-based recommendations. 43. WHO guidelines address the management of health complications resulting from female genital mutilation. 44. The World Report on Disability (2011) provides a comprehensive overview of global disability issues. 45. WHO's Global Disability Action Plan (2014–2021) aims to improve health outcomes for people with disabilities. 46. WHO recommendations on adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights emphasize evidence-based interventions. 47. WHO guidelines for antenatal care promote a positive pregnancy experience for women. 48. Standards for improving maternal and newborn care quality in health facilities are outlined in WHO's recommendations. 49. WHO guidelines for the treatment of sexually transmitted infections, including syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydia, and gonorrhea, provide evidence-based approaches. 50. WHO guidelines for managing stress-related conditions and psychological first aid for field workers are available. 51. Psychosocial interventions for treating behavioral and emotional disorders in children and adolescents are outlined in WHO's mhGAP guidelines. 52. WHO's global imperative for suicide prevention highlights strategies for reducing suicide rates worldwide. 53. Pharmacological interventions for somatoform disorders in children and adolescents are addressed in WHO's evidence-based recommendations. 54. WHO emphasizes the importance of delivering quality health services as part of universal health coverage. 55. Guidelines for iodine thyroid blocking in radiological and nuclear emergencies are provided by WHO. 56. WHO's health emergency and disaster risk management framework offers guidance for preparedness and response. 57. School-based interventions for reducing suicide attempts among young people are outlined in WHO's recommendations. 58. WHO provides a resource for teachers and school staff on preventing suicide among students. 59. WHO guidelines for preventing allergy and allergic asthma are based on expert consultations. 60. Strategies for preventing violence through nurturing relationships between children and caregivers are outlined in WHO's recommendations. 61. The Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST) manual is available for use in primary care settings. 62. WHO's guidelines for preventive chemotherapy to control soil-transmitted helminth infections in at-risk populations are provided. 63. WHO's recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening emphasize the integration of technology into health programs. 64. A framework for national health policies, strategies, and plans is outlined in WHO's consultation document. 65. WHO's Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) manual supports the development of national adolescent health strategies. 66. WHO's final report on equity and universal health coverage emphasizes evidence-informed decision-making processes. 67. A global review of health-promoting school policies and standards is in progress, as documented by WHO. This transformation provides a clear and professional summary of the references and guidelines, maintaining the specificity and context of each item.
